c05d1a4fa3.q: How did Dave Wilson transition from lorry driving to owning Drive Green Vehicle Services?
c05d1a4fa3.a: Dave Wilson started Drive Green Vehicle Services eight years ago while still lorry driving, beginning with carbon cleaning using hydrogen technology after investing in equipment to pay off debt. He set up a Facebook page with no connections in the trade and gradually shifted focus to DPF cleaning after learning about it from a mechanic, eventually quitting lorry driving after realizing he could earn a week's wages in a single day doing DPF cleans.
c05d1a4fa3.e: From Lorry Driver to Award-Winning Garage Owner | Dave Wilson, Drive Green
c05d1a4fa3.rq: You need to be naive to start, don't you? I'm quite a determined person. If I want to find something out, I will bend over backwards to find it out.

ebd1d8228a.q: What was Dave Wilson's first carbon cleaning job and how did he find his first customer?
ebd1d8228a.a: Dave Wilson's first customer was a silver Jeep Cherokee found through a poster he paid to place at a local car wash. He dropped the initial price from £75 to £50 for the job and even did a couple of cars for free initially, borrowing tools from friends when he lacked proper equipment like jubilee clips and hose pliers.

cb2c18ebc5.q: How did Dave Wilson learn DPF cleaning without formal training?
cb2c18ebc5.a: Dave Wilson learned DPF cleaning through YouTube research, particularly following a channel called On Car Cleaner. He initially invested £300 in additional equipment despite earning only about £600 per week, then purchased a £600 diagnostics tool to handle engine light errors, eventually discovering through trial and error the secret menu process that allowed him to properly reset fault codes.

c6385d7668.q: What made Dave Wilson decide to leave lorry driving and commit full-time to Drive Green?
c6385d7668.a: After being let go from his second lorry driving job due to cost-cutting by his employer, Dave was mistreated at a new haulage company and decided to pursue his business full-time. His father's terminal illness also influenced his decision, as he wanted to remain available for family emergencies rather than committing to long-distance lorry driving that might separate him from his dying father.

e1745f7a01.q: What was Dave Wilson's financial situation when starting Drive Green Vehicle Services?
e1745f7a01.a: Dave Wilson initially invested two thousand pounds in carbon cleaning equipment while earning decent money as a lorry driver but spending equally well, leaving him in a precarious financial position. He had two children and accumulated debt that motivated him to start the side business, though he remained concerned about basic household bills and caring for his family during his transition to full-time business ownership.
